components.name: Transmit Button
components.description: The singular command that sends a composed operation.
components.css: .ds-send { min-height: 50px; padding: 9px 14px; color: #1b2422; background: #d99235; border: 0; border-radius: 7px; box-shadow: 0 3px 0 #945d1e; font: 700 15px 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background-color 140ms ease-out, transform 90ms ease-out, box-shadow 90ms ease-out; } .ds-send:hover { background: #eeaa50; } .ds-send:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #8ab9d3; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-send:active { transform: translateY(2px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #945d1e; }

components.name: Protocol Readout

components.css: .ds-readout { padding: 18px 20px; color: #17231b; background: #c9d4ad; border: 2px solid #111716; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: inset 0 3px 10px rgba(24,38,29,.24); font-family: Consolas, monospace; } .ds-readout small { display: block; color: #53604e; font: 800 10px 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-readout strong { display: block; margin-top: 8px; font-size: 18px; }

narrative.overview: The interface borrows the operational confidence of a serious handheld scientific calculator: a durable dark chassis, a broad low-glare readout, tightly grouped controls, and keys that communicate function through position as much as color. Protocol detail remains part of the working surface.
keyCharacteristics: Explicit labels and persistent connection state
Instrument-grade density with generous hit targets

rules.name: The Indicator Rule
rules.body: Saturated color communicates action or live state; it is not ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Wire values and device output always use monospace; explanatory text never needs to imitate a terminal.

dos: Do make the current port state and transmitted byte sequence visible at all times.
Do group operation keys by function and preserve familiar mathematical labels.
Do make keyboard focus as legible as pointer hover.
donts: Don't turn every section into a floating card.
Don't use glow, glass, or decorative gradients in place of instrument structure.
Don't hide protocol errors behind generic failure messages.
